title: Spring flow width trends were uncertain at three Arctic gauges in 31 common certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether the central 60% of April-July discharge spread over more days at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and 31 common complete certified years in 1980-2011, excluding 2000. Width trends were +1.199, +0.633 and +0.769 days per decade. Approximate 95% family limits were -0.210 to +2.741, -1.178 to +2.335 and -1.208 to +2.868. Thus the main test did not establish broadening at any gauge. Ob had a positive April-August check but a near-zero estimate with a 1990 start. The quantile width removes positive amplitude scaling but remains sensitive to background flow and window edges. This extends prior timing-gap tests with a spread metric; data overlap and do not give independent confirmation. Short records, regulation, fixed windows and conditional block uncertainty limit inference. The package gives code, aggregate results, source hashes, a plan, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit. Raw and annual record tables remain external.
